Israeli ⁠forces have killed ⁠at least six Palestinians, including a father and his 13-year-old son, in the Gaza Strip, according to local health sources.
Three people were killed on Tuesday in an Israeli air attack on the Ghubain family home in Gaza City’s Daraj area. A father and son were killed in a separate air attack on a tent in the city’s Zeitoun neighbourhood, and a man was killed by Israeli gunfire in the southern city of Khan Younis.

Gaza continues to face regular Israeli attacks despite last year’s “ceasefire”. In fact, more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed by Israel in the besieged enclave since the United States-brokered truce agreement, according to the territory’s ‌Ministry of Health.
More than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel’s genocidal war ‌on ‌Gaza since October 7, 2023, the ministry said.
The killings come as the first strong storm of the season over the weekend flooded about 70,000 tents in Gaza within 12 hours, killing at least five people and causing about $3m in damage, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.

Bullet holes are seen in the coffee garden window at the Main Market Square in Krakow, Poland on November 9, 2026 [AFP]By Al Jazeera Staff and ReutersPublished On 10 Nov 202610 Nov 2026
A Polish man who opened fire in Krakow city’s main square and killed six people on Saturday visited websites about Norwegian white-supremacist killer Anders Behring Breivik, according to Poland’s justice minister.
Waldemar Zurek said on Tuesday that there was “a very strong indication of right-wing extremism” behind the gunman’s actions that shook the nation on November 7.

Investigators also found in his possessions a Gadsden flag – a US Civil War-era flag featuring a rattlesnake on a yellow background that is often linked to the US far right, the minister added.
Prosecutors named the suspect as 24-year-old factory worker Michal Oksinski. He died in hospital on Monday after being shot and arrested by police minutes after they said he opened fire from his car in Krakow’s historic main square, a popular tourist destination.
Zurek said that a silencer, a muzzle device used to reduce the noise of a gun, was found in the car used by the killer.Two women mourn next to a makeshift memorial close to the Main Market Square in Krakow, Poland, two days after a gunman opened fire on November 9, 2026 [AFP]
The bodies of Oksinski’s father, mother and sister were found in their family home on Saturday. Officials say they were also likely killed by Oksinski.

View of a damaged train car while police officers gather at the site of a deadly collision between two passenger trains near al-Ayyat village in Giza Governorate, south of Cairo, Egypt, November 8, 2026 [Mohamed Abd El Ghany/Reuters]By Mohamed KhayyalPublished On 10 Nov 202610 Nov 2026
A deadly train collision in the outskirts of the Egyptian capital Cairo, which killed at least seven people and injured more than 125 others according to the country’s Ministry of Health and Population, has ignited a wave of parliamentary and political demands for accountability. The disaster raises urgent questions about the effect of the millions of dollars the Egyptian state has poured into upgrading the railway network and whether those investments are genuinely improving passenger safety.
A train travelling between Giza and Fayoum on Sunday ran into the back of another train on the Cairo-to-Aswan route, causing the latter to derail onto a countryside road in al-Ayyat district. Following the crash, President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”.

Diplomatic efforts to end the United States-Israel war on Iran have gathered pace, potentially reducing the chance of another round of intense conflict.
US President Donald Trump and Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani hailed positive closed-door talks at the White House on Monday, with Trump saying he considers the war “effectively” at an end.

But amid talk of peace, both sides have boasted that their militaries are ready and Iran has come under attack.
The US “is fully locked and loaded with the best equipment ever made”, Trump said, but added there would likely be no reason to use it as negotiations with Tehran are “going very well”.
Iran pointed to the possibility of a diplomatic solution while maintaining a deterrence posture.
On Tuesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the war would “not end either through military means or by increasing sanctions”, but only through “using the language of respect”.
The comment came a day after Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had hinted at an openness to negotiations, telling the country’s leadership to end the “no war, no peace” reality.
“We can hold talks with dignity and bring the matter to an end with dignity,” Pezeshkian said.

Russia and Ukraine have attacked one another’s ports this year, choking off grain and oilseed exports that feed import-dependent countries in Africa and South Asia, and leaving India short of sunflower oil.
